entry.title: UIFramework v1.2.0: UIFramework v1.2.0
entry.content:
Fixes from an audit of the whole framework, and the logo on the About page.

Added

  • The UIFramework logo on the About page. Faint in the bottom right corner, like a watermark, so the window shows it is the original framework: brighter under the mouse, its tooltip names the framework's version, a click opens its page. It sits under the content, never over a link, in the dark or the light version for the theme.

Fixed

  • Help under fields in named rows. A button or switch beside other fields lines up with them again, a button's help line goes under the row instead of stretching its column, and every help line keeps a gap to the next field.
  • List files are never written over by mistake. A list kept in a file of its own that the game holds open stops the save with the reason, instead of counting as damaged and being written from the window. A list that could not be read when the window opened shows its defaults, says so behind the red i, and is not written from that window.
  • Reset page leaves lists in files of their own, transient and read-only settings alone, as Reset all does. Both dialogs say what they do: Reset all saves at once and keeps the file as it was as .bak.
  • A game setting called darkMode, DarkMode, egg, Egg or rainbow is no longer taken for the window's theme and removed from the game's file.
  • A condition such as !mode=free always held. The red i now names it, with the way to write it (mode!=free).
  • A cooldown that reads a key no setting has is named behind the red i; before, only a line in the log said so on every save.
  • The version check no longer fails ("Value cannot be null") for a game whose version is no number.
  • Add row in a list with a search typed clears the search, so the new row shows.
  • Host block: UiHost.Handle clears the window's arguments before it calls the game's handler, so an action the handler runs is not taken for a window request. Games get this with their next host-block update.
  • The demo game no longer names the framework's repository as its releases, which showed an update pill in every demo window after each framework release.
  • Docs: Getting-Started's snippet for an existing game declares its three constants and reads its settings; the table snippet has the userCooldown its cooldown reads; the DLL goes into lib\<version>\; what ActionName is for. Customize: How to play, Log and About sit at the foot of the page list; help and about lines translate.

entry.title: Classic Chat Gamble v25.1.0: A tour of the window, and the window in German
entry.content:
Gambles play as before. The settings window reads in English or German and runs on UIFramework for streamer.bot 1.0.0: the settings window shows you around on its first open, and problems it finds sit behind one red i in its header.

Added

  • A tour of the settings window. The first time the window opens, a short tour rings one part after the other (the pages, saving, the customise mode) and says what it does; the ? at the top right shows it again.
  • UIFramework 1.0.0. Problems the window finds sit behind a red i in its header instead of on the About or Log page, and How to play, Log and About sit together at the foot of the page list. The settings action offers the new framework on its next open.

Changed

  • The chat messages are in configs.json. Every setting now sits in one file, as in the other games. An old messages.json moves in on the first run of the game or of the settings window: each message goes into configs.json under its new name (one set to null becomes an empty message, which still sends nothing), and the file stays beside it as messages.json.migrated.
  • When the window opens on the numbers of another fairness stop, the slider moves there without a filled in note in the footer; the note is for a stop you pick.
  • Fixed bet only in Fixed mode. Fixed bet under Channel points shows while the bet mode is Fixed; before, it stood there greyed out in the other modes.
  • The settings action is UIFramework's generic stub. [CCG] - Settings carries no layout and no game code any more: the game action declares its window (pages, pills, the log, help and about, the !gamble cooldowns) beside its settings table and answers the window itself (the fairness stops, the odds, a test roll, the check before saving). Needs UIFramework 0.9.2 or newer; the stub fetches it.
  • German. With the window's language set to de (the pencil, then Sprache), every setting, section, page and message of the window reads in German. The help and about pages stay English.
  • The settings action is UIFramework's stub 0.2.0. When the game action hangs, the settings window waits 30 seconds for its answer, then carries on and can be closed; before, it waited for good. A game that has not described itself for a minute no longer locks the settings until Streamer.bot restarts: the next run opens the window.
  • The host block is UIFramework's current one (1.0.0). It names every type in full, so it no longer depends on the action's using lines, and it can declare a tour of the window. Nothing changes in the window.
  • A chance, multiplier or percentage written as NaN or infinity into configs.json still falls back the way it did; the new host block alone would read it as 0.

entry.title: Battleship Game v2.2.0: A tour of the window, an overlay demo and Free game from chat
entry.content:
The overlay can play a made-up battle to place and style it, moderators switch Free game from chat, and every finished battle fires a trigger your own actions can use. On UIFramework for streamer.bot 1.0.0, the settings window shows you around on its first open, and problems it finds sit behind one red i in its header.

Added

  • A tour of the settings window. The first time the window opens, a short tour rings one part after the other (the pages, saving, the customise mode) and says what it does; the ? at the top right shows it again.
  • UIFramework 1.0.0. Problems the window finds sit behind a red i in its header instead of on the About or Log page, and How to play, Log and About sit together at the foot of the page list. The settings action offers the new framework on its next open.

📺 Overlay

  • Try the demo. A new button on the Overlay page opens the overlay in your browser, playing a short made-up battle in the saved look (a miss, a sunk destroyer, the Admiral finding your cruiser, the enemy fleet sunk), without Streamer.bot. With ?demo=1 on the overlay's address, OBS plays it the same way, to place and size the source.
  • Show a sample round. The button beside it plays that battle once on every overlay that is open, the one in OBS included, so you can check where it sits and how it looks; then the overlay goes back to no battle. Not while a real battle runs. The overlay is version 17 and replaces an older copy on the next command, keeping that one as a .bak; an overlay already open in OBS reloads itself within ten seconds.

🆓 Free game from chat

  • Two moderator commands. !SetFreeBattleship turns Free game on and !EndFreeBattleship turns it off (they come with the import, disabled and set to the Moderators group). The switch is written into the settings file, so the window's pill shows it, and chat gets the new Started and Ended messages (Messages page, Free game). An action of your own can do the same with an Execute C# Method on StartFreeGame or EndFreeGame of the game action.
  • Two more custom triggers. BSG: Free Game Start and BSG: Free Game End fire whenever Free game is switched that way.

🪟 Settings window

  • The settings action is UIFramework's stub 0.2.0. When the game action hangs, the settings window waits 30 seconds for its answer, then carries on and can be closed; before, it waited for good. A game that has not described itself for a minute no longer locks the settings until Streamer.bot restarts: the next run opens the window.

  • The host block is UIFramework's current one (1.0.0). It names every type in full, so it no longer depends on the action's using lines, and it can declare a tour of the window. Nothing changes in the window.

  • German. With the window's language set to de (the pencil, then Sprache), every setting, section, page and message of the window reads in German. The help and about pages, the summaries and the presets' status line stay English.

  • The settings action is UIFramework's generic stub. [BG] - .Settings carries no layout and no code of its own any more: the game action declares its window (pages, the log, help and about, the cooldowns of !battleship) beside its settings table and answers the window itself. Reset the leaderboard now, Set the overlay up in OBS and Add to OBS now answer with what happened instead of "queued", and a save puts the Click to Fire settings on a live overlay as before. Needs UIFramework 0.9.2 or newer; the stub fetches it.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers. Every finished battle fires a trigger (Custom > Chat Game > Battleship Game): BSG: Battle Won, BSG: Battle Lost, BSG: Battle Timed Out or BSG: Battle Stopped for a solo battle, BSG: Chat Battle Settled for the chat's battle, BSG: Duel Settled for a team duel, and BSG: Battle Settled for every one of them. The trigger carries the battle as arguments: battleOutcome (the log's result: WIN, LOSS, TIMEOUT, NO-SHOW, STOPPED), battleMode (solo, chat or duel), battleUser, battleUserId, battlePlatform, battleTrigger (fire, timeout or stop), battleBoard, battleShots, battleHits, battleAccuracy, battleShipsSunk, battleShipsLost, battleNet (the battle's total, or a duel's pot), battleWinner (a duel's winning side) and battleCurrency. GetLastBattleResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands the same arguments to any other action.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.0.0: UIFramework v1.0.0
entry.content:
The first stable release: the settings window every chat game of aaskjer's runs on (Blackjack, Battleship, Classic Chat Gamble, Hangman, High-Low, RhymeTime, Slot Machine, Trivia), with a tour of itself, its problems behind one red button, and a Log page that reads old and new log lines alike. From here on, the host block and the settings action change only in ways the CHANGELOG says, and a release that breaks a game needs a new major version.

  • Problems behind a red "i". What the game declares that does not fit, and what fails while the window is open (a page that cannot be built, a handler that throws, a failed save, an unreadable layout file), no longer show as a banner and a list on the Log or About page. A red i appears in the header instead; a click opens a panel that lists them in two groups, the failures with their time, and Copy puts the whole list on the clipboard for a bug report. Esc, the close button or a click beside it closes it. Every line still goes to Streamer.bot's log. The status line's "Something went wrong" points at the i. Preview: -windowshots <folder> -problems photographs the window with the i, then with its panel open.
  • A tour stop to try out. Tip(target, title, text, act: true) lets the user use the ringed part while the stop is up: clicks go through the ring to it, keys reach it, the rest of the window stays out of reach, and the ring follows the part as it grows (a Try button's answer). The note says Try it yourself. The demo game's Roll stop is one.
  • How to play, Log and About at the foot of the rail. The three sit together at the bottom of the page list, in this order, whatever order a game declares them in; a game's own bottom page goes above them.
  • The Log page reads more. Older lines in columns (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss RESULT user [R1|id] Key: value | ...) show their time, result, player, round and fields instead of an empty row. A column may name several keys ("Word|Word,Word was"): the first the line has is shown. A value in one pair of single quotes loses them. Results read with a capital per part (Game-Over, Hit-Lettr), and column headers and the empty text translate through the game's Tx like every declared text.
  • Every chat game has a tour and the current host block; High-Low and RhymeTime have a Log page now, and Hangman's log fills every column (hosts/).

entry.title: UIFramework v0.9.13: UIFramework v0.9.13 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Spanish and every language offered, neutral credits, saving that keeps what the game wrote, a sturdier loader (stub 0.2.0), and the review's findings fixed.

  • Spanish. conventions/lang/es.json translates every known key, page, placeholder and window text, and the short wordings German translates.

  • Every language is offered. The language picker lists every language there are texts for, by its own name (English, Deutsch, Español): the DLL's files, a file in UIFramework\lang\ beside Streamer.bot (a new language or corrections, without a release), and the languages a game brings texts for. A game without texts of its own gets what the conventions translate. A game that names its window's language has no picker.

  • A game can translate the window itself for a language the framework lacks: Ui(key, text) and Ph(placeholder, help) in Lang.

  • A relabelled known key keeps the game's wording where the conventions do not translate it; before, a language without a conventions file showed the conventions' English label over the game's own.

  • Neutral credits. The framework names no author: a game without credits shows none, and every About page ends with the links conventions/keys.json lists (about.links): the UIFramework page on aaskjer.github.io, Streamer.bot and Report something that looks wrong (the game's issues when it names its repository, else the framework's). About(defaultLinks: false) leaves them out; authorLink does nothing any more.

  • More said to a game's author: a known key declared as another kind of value (it would still take the conventions' limits, old keys and translations), a section split by another on its page (its heading would show twice), an icon name the framework does not know (it shows a dot instead of the word).

  • Fixes to the fixes: a request hung in the game action no longer blocks the next ones (taking over a window and reopening one work again); a list moving into its own file survives the open-time theme move and Reset all, and Reset all leaves lists in their own files; whole numbers stay exact past 2^53; the next save also writes a switch, dropdown or slider shown other than stored; a hidden number box without a number keeps its value; a list file unreadable at save keeps the window's copy of its untouched lists; UiSettings.Load survives a bad path; an older DLL gets "no answer" as before instead of the stub's marker; the sample thousands separator follows the window's language.

  • The host block needs no usings. stub/HostSchema.cs names every type in full (Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JObject, System.IO.File, ...), so it compiles in any game action whatever its using lines say, right below them, at the end or inside CPHInline, and a game's own usings can no longer clash with it (a Path or Formatting of another namespace). Before, the game's action had to bring seven usings, and the file pasted alone into a new Execute Code failed with some 150 errors ("The type or namespace name 'JObject' could not be found"). tools/check-stub.ps1 compiles the block alone now. A game's present block keeps working; tools/update-host-block.ps1 brings the new one, and takes only what stands between the template's markers.

  • Getting-Started is copy and paste. Five steps to the running demo game, each with the ready file to paste (examples/DemoGame/DemoGame.cs, stub/Stub.cs) and nothing to change, what to do when a step fails, then how to make it your own game and how to add the block to a game you already have. The demo game carries its host block below the usings like every game, and names its command by its text (C("!roll", ...)), so a !roll made by hand gets the cooldowns too.

  • Twitch emotes show without a Twitch login. A fresh Streamer.bot has no Twitch token, so the window could not ask the Twitch API and Kappa, LUL and the other global emotes stayed without a picture. Their ids now ship in conventions/emotes/twitch.json; with a login the window still asks Twitch itself, for the channel's emotes too. tools/update-twitch-emotes.ps1 refreshes the list.

  • The coins icon shows. A page with the conventions' coins icon (Points & Bets) showed an empty box: 🪙 is missing from the emoji font WPF draws with, so it is 💰 now.

  • Docs with pictures, and the conventions published. Getting-Started, Customize, Schema and the README show the window; docs/Conventions.md lists the standard pages, known keys, placeholders and language files, and explains how to add a language. tools/conventions-doc.ps1 keeps its tables current, and CI checks them.

  • German windows show the cooldown senders again. The Messages page's "send as bot" and "send as action" switches for the cooldown messages were missing in German: the message groups are translated ("Abklingzeit"), the cooldown group was looked for in English. It is found in the window's language now.

  • A game handler that hangs no longer freezes the window (stub 0.2.0). A request that has started gets 30 seconds, then the window carries on without its answer; before, it waited for good and could not be closed. A game that has not sent its schema for a minute no longer locks its settings until Streamer.bot restarts: the next run opens the window.

  • A declined save leaves nothing behind. The window's values go into a draft; only a save that is written takes them over. Before, a save declined at a warning kept them in the window's copy, and after a theme or language switch they looked saved while the file still held the old ones.

  • A number pulled into its limits is written. A value outside a field's min/max (or no number at all) that the window shows as its limit or default is written with the next save, also when the user did not touch that field; so is what the game's clamp changed. Before, the box said 25 and the game kept reading 50.

  • A save that cannot read the settings file stops and says why, instead of writing every list file from the copy the window opened with. A list moving out of the settings file into its own lands there with the first save.

  • Import reads like the settings file: old keys with their factors on any Windows language (an old 0.18 is 18 % on a German system too), old keys inside an object, the current key winning. It lays the import over the file as it is now and writes only the lists it brings.

  • Reset all keeps read-only settings and those on pages the user hid, and the game hears of the lists in their own files as they are, not as defaults.

  • First install checks minHostStub too (stub 0.2.0): a release that needs a newer settings action is not installed by an older game; "0.2.0.0" no longer counts as newer than "0.2.0".

  • Loader details (stub 0.2.0): a DLL that no longer matches its hash is set aside as .broken and its version offered again, and an installed file that is not the published one is fetched anew; the hash file is written before the DLL. Every game uses the UIFramework another game already loaded, so two versions never run side by side, and the log says which runs. One request to the game at a time, so two runs never read each other's answer; the run serving a reopened window hands the one-window flag back. A latest.json version that is no plain number is refused in the release check too. A cooldown above a day is set to a day with a line in the log.

  • Host block: UiSettings.Long reads a whole number exactly (no detour through a double), and Load never throws, also on a path with invalid characters.

  • Conditions compare what is stored, shown or not. A percent compares as its fraction (reshuffleThreshold>=0.5 for 50 %), a duration in seconds, an "unlimited" 0 as the number it is saved as; a field hidden by the user no longer compares differently. !list holds for an empty list.

  • The check names a comparison that never holds: <, <=, >, >= against text, or on a field that holds no number. A slider on a scale (min, max, step) is no longer reported as "without options".

  • A huge number in the settings file breaks nothing: a whole number with more digits than a long reads as the largest value instead of failing the page.

  • Saving is not stopped by fields it never writes: a Try field left empty, or a number hidden by a showWhen or its section's condition. Fields on another page are still checked.

  • A page pattern leaves the sender switches and the log switch where they are, so no key gets two fields that overwrite each other on save. A page naming one by key is listed as a problem.

  • The placeholder chips' tooltips follow a language switch; a host's own help is kept.

  • Percent fields keep their decimals. Leaving the box rewrites only a number outside its range, to that limit; 12.345 stays 12.345. A value in the file that is no number shows the default instead of an empty box that blocks saving.

  • Customise keeps rows together. A field dropped at the top or bottom of a field that shares a line goes above or below the whole line, not between its members. The log page's "log file per day" switch is greyed in the customise mode, which has no Save.

  • A slider's kept value goes on Reset page and set also when the slider already sits on the stop it is put on; its label follows.

  • German windows have no English left in the customise tag "hidden", the empty-page note, the path and colour tooltips, an action's "done"/"failed" and the table's "Nothing here yet"/"Read again".

  • A layout file another program holds is not lost. It is read again a few times; if it is still held, the window starts from the defaults for once and does not write over it. Only a file that is no JSON goes to .broken.

  • Numbers the same on every Windows: decimal boxes take a minus where the setting allows negatives and refuse a paste that is no number; a list cell refuses "1,000" like the table (also when saved while it has the focus) and shows "2.5", not "2,5"; a value an action sets finds its option on a German system.

  • Smaller fixes: emote pictures load over HTTPS only; update-host-block sees a change in letter case; the release workflow refuses a pre-release tag before publishing and keeps the published DLL on a re-run; the demo's dice are thread-safe.

  • Settings action (stub 0.2.0): a game's answer is unset from Streamer.bot's globals as soon as it is read, so the Twitch token in the emote sources no longer stays visible in the variables. A DLL saved from a browser loads (it was refused as "downloaded from the internet"). When the newest installed DLL cannot be loaded, the next older one opens the window. The hash a download was checked with is kept beside the DLL and checked on every load. A release that names a higher minHostStub is not offered. A game takes this with its next release, by pasting the new stub/Stub.cs as its settings action.

  • Nothing unchecked from latest.json. The settings action installs no release without a sha256, fetches the DLL over https:// only and refuses a version that is not a version number before it becomes a folder name.

  • The release check no longer holds the window up to 10 s. Offline (unreachable, timed out) it does not try the CDN after the API; a network sign-in page instead of latest.json falls back to the CDN.

  • A second click brings the window to the front. While a game's window is open (or still opening), another run of its settings action neither asks the game nor checks for a release again, and leaves the first run's queue alone.

  • The hint for a hand-fetched DLL shows offline too. Its example path no longer fails on <version> when latest.json cannot be read.

  • A save keeps what it did not change. The window writes the settings file as it is at that moment with the fields the user changed laid over it, instead of the copy it read when it opened: a viewer added from chat, a question suggested from chat or a status the game wrote while the window was open survive a save that did not touch them. A list kept in a file of its own is written only when its list changed.

  • A damaged list file is kept. One that cannot be read is copied to .broken before the window writes over it, and a list file (a JSON array) now gets its .bak on every save like the settings file.

  • Numbers keep their decimals. A number field shows up to ten decimals instead of two, so 0.005 no longer shows, and saves back, as 0.01, nor 0.001 as 0.

  • The language switch asks first. In a locked window, picking another language with unsaved changes asks to save them, as the theme button does, instead of dropping them.

  • Numbers the same on every Windows. Option values, dropdowns, sliders, text fields and the host block's UiSettings.String/Double/Long read and write numbers with a point, so a German system no longer turns 0.5 into "0,5"; Long no longer overflows on a huge stored value.

  • A bad stored value no longer breaks a page. A number field whose value is no number shows its default, a number stored as text ("0,5" too) is read, and a fraction in a whole-number field is shown instead of cut.

  • min/max hold for int, long and duration. A value outside is saved as the nearest limit, and the field shows what was saved; a min below 0 lets the field take a minus.

  • A big default makes a long field. A whole-number default beyond an int (also where the conventions say int) is no longer cut to 2147483647 on save.

  • Dropdowns and stop sliders keep an unknown value. A stored value none of the options has stays as an extra entry, selected, and is saved back unchanged instead of the first option.

  • Number columns take numbers. A table cell of an int, long or double column takes digits (and a minus, a decimal mark) only, and a cell that is no number goes back to what it held instead of saving 0.

  • readOnly in both spellings; more for the host block. readOnly and readonly are read on a setting and a column. S() takes readOnly, step and group. A column flag right after the kind ("wins|int|readonly", "face|emote|twitch") is a flag, not the label.

  • null hides any sender switch. An explicit null in senders hides useBot, sendAction, cooldownUseBot, cooldownSendAction and cooldownGroup, as documented; before only numberSeparator obeyed.

  • Conditions. !key holds while a switch is off or a field is empty. A gate the window does not show is read from its saved value instead of counting as met. A field the user's layout moves to another section takes that section's condition. An answer box that moves under its row hides with its button.

  • Typed decimals are not guessed. "1,000" or "1.000,5" in a decimal field is refused as ambiguous instead of read as 1.

  • A damaged layout file is kept. uiframework.layout.json that is not JSON is copied to .broken and logged; a value of the wrong type in it ("order": "2") reads as not set instead of breaking the window.

  • A check that got no answer asks. When the game did not answer validate (a timeout, a disabled action), the window asks whether to save unchecked instead of taking it for "no problems" (stub 0.2.0).

  • A hung game action no longer locks the window. The window can be opened again while a request still hangs; a request the window gave up on is skipped instead of run late (stub 0.2.0). An error in a click handler is logged and shown in the status line instead of closing the window.

  • Emote sources are asked once per window, not once per emote cell.

  • Rebuilds no longer leak. A section heading follows its fields through a binding; every rebuild (language, theme, customise mode) kept the old page alive before.

  • Two windows at once keep their own theme, accent, rainbow and language.

  • Cooldowns are set safely (stub 0.2.0): a misnamed key leaves the cooldown as it is instead of setting 0, one command that fails leaves the others set, and the game always hears of the save.

  • The stub writes the layout file carefully (stub 0.2.0): only on a change, atomically, never over a file it could not read. TLS 1.2 is added without pinning the process; the download mutex is honoured; the dialogs name the current version's folder.

  • Customise-mode drops check that the field or page came from this window; a message template can no longer be dropped on another page through the rail, a field dropped on its own page stays where it is, and a field moved to another page leaves its old row.

  • Release workflow builds the tag's own commit, carries minHostStub over and never takes latest.json back.

  • Docs: the usings the host block needs; the nested RunAction pitfall. tools/update-host-block.ps1 keeps a .bak and refuses to drop lines of the game's own unless -Force.

  • Smaller: Ctrl+S does nothing in the customise mode; a name typed into a name list but not entered counts as a change when closing; an answer with only set/status keeps the result panel's previous lines.

  • Text keeps its spaces. A string field saves what was typed, spaces at either end included (" | ", "🎲 "); names, paths, colours and tokens are still trimmed.

  • Durations in minutes and hours. A duration with unit min or h is typed and shown in that unit and stored in seconds (1.5 min is 90); min/max stay seconds.

  • A greyed-out field looks it on every kind: a requires that does not hold also dims the field.

  • German follows the game's own wording. A conventions key the game gave a label (or help) of its own is translated by the game's Tx for that wording; without one the conventions' German for the key is shown, as before. K(key, label) without a help keeps the conventions' help.

  • stats and channelPoints pages have an icon and a place in the order (icon name gift is new).

  • Reset all keeps what the window does not show: hidden settings and keys it has no field for.

  • A page pattern leaves a moved field alone. A field the user moved to another page is not claimed back by overlay*; a claimed field's page is the claiming one, and a template a page claims by key leaves the Messages picker.

  • More checks: a section condition for a section no setting is in, an old key that is another setting's key.

  • Aliases: an old key that is a setting of its own keeps its value instead of being moved and reset; a dotted alias feeds shared keys too and its old value goes also when the canonical key is in the file.

  • Host block: UiSettings.Load falls back to the .bak of the last save on a damaged file and says so (Problem, FromBackup, an optional log); a relative path starts in the Streamer.bot folder.

  • Docs: the game action's code is its last sub-action.

entry.title: High-Low Game v2.1.0: Higher, lower or the same, guess to find out
entry.content:
The first release of High-Low Game on GitHub. There is always a number from 1 to 100 waiting; viewers guess whether the next one is higher, lower or the same, on Twitch, YouTube and Kick. The settings window is UIFramework for streamer.bot, the window all of these chat games share, in English or German.

🎲 The game

  • A number from the start. The game draws one for each platform when Streamer.bot starts, so nobody has to run !highlowsetup first. Moderators can still draw and announce a fresh one with it.
  • !high, !low and !equal. A correct high or low pays the win amount, a wrong one costs nothing; !equal pays double and costs the win amount when wrong. The answer names both numbers.
  • Scoreboards. !hlgsession, !hlgalltime and !hlgpersonal, with the broadcaster and the bot account left out if you want.

🎫 Channel points on Twitch

  • Three rewards, one each for high, low and equal. Paste their IDs on the Channel points page; the import already carries the reward trigger.
  • Stakes: Cost and Fixed spend the channel points and pay a correct guess in points, Input takes a bet in the viewer's own points (all, half, 2k, …), Free plays like the chat commands. Minimum and maximum bet apply.
  • Refunds. A redemption that does not end in a guess is refunded, a played one is marked as fulfilled.

🪟 One settings window for all the chat games

  • Downloaded on first open. [HLG] - .Settings is UIFramework's small settings stub. The first time you open it, it offers to download UIFramework.dll from GitHub (checked against its published SHA-256) or to show the folder it belongs in. Nothing is fetched without that click; newer releases are offered when you open the window, never forced.
  • English or German. The pencil, then Sprache: every setting, section, page and message reads in German.
  • Customise mode. Rename, reorder, hide and move pages and fields, pick the accent colour. It lives in uiframework.layout.json next to HLG-Settings.json and survives every import.
  • Cooldowns per command, written onto the Streamer.bot commands when you save, and every chat line editable with a live preview.

🔔 For your own actions

  • Custom triggers (Custom > Chat Game > High-Low Game): HLG: Guess Won, HLG: Guess Lost and HLG: Guess Settled for every guess, HLG: New Number when !highlowsetup draws one.
  • The guess as arguments: guessOutcome, guessUser, guessPlatform, guessGuess, guessPreviousNumber, guessNewNumber, guessMode, guessStake, guessAmount, guessPreviousPoints, guessNewPoints, guessCurrency, guessFree and more. GetLastGuessResult, run with an Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action, hands them to any other action.

🆓 Free mode

  • A switch on the Game page, or !SetFreeHighLow / !EndFreeHighLow from chat (moderators). Nobody wins or loses points, the guesses still count. The two commands come with the import, disabled: enable them in Streamer.bot's Commands tab if you want them.
  • HLG: Free Game Start and HLG: Free Game End fire when it is switched, from chat or by an Execute C# Method on StartFreeGame or EndFreeGame, and chat gets a Started and an Ended line.

💰 Points

  • Works with Currency Core by StreamUP and LOYALTY POINTS by tawmae: whichever is installed names the points variable and the points name. Anything else works too; name its variable on the Game page.

Installing

Import HighLowGame.sb below, or the import string, then open the settings with the Test trigger of [HLG] - .Settings. The setup guide walks through every page.

Coming from an earlier copy of the game? Import over the existing actions: HLG-Settings.json stays where it is, old setting names are read until the window saves them under the new ones, and old cooldown messages with {0} and {1} still work. Trovo support and the per-platform switches are gone; leave a platform out by unticking its source on the commands.
